brown.title: Noam Brown’s post
brown.summary: Claims human Go skill improved after AlphaGo and speculates about a similar pattern in mathematics. The attached figure displays decision quality.
brown.limit: A social claim and chart share, not an independent study. Replies and quote-post access are incomplete.

brownsource.title: Brown’s source reply
brownsource.summary: Links Henrik Karlsson’s Go article as the source.
brownsource.limit: The linked article currently resolves to a page-not-found screen.

anpaure.title: anpaure’s critical reply
anpaure.summary: Objects that the reported improvement could reflect memorized openings and links a player critique.
anpaure.limit: A compressed account of the critique, not an independently tested result.

nagaraj.title: Abhishek Nagaraj’s reply
nagaraj.summary: Emphasizes younger players and links the Choi–Kang–Kim–Kim paper.
nagaraj.limit: Does not independently establish the finding or address enjoyment.

choi.title: Choi et al.: human decision-making
choi.summary: Reports improved move quality around public engine access, especially early in the game; younger and less-skilled players show stronger benefits on the studied outcomes.
choi.locator: Abstract; §§3–5, especially research design and stage comparisons
choi.limit: Primary window: first 30 moves. No individual engine-use data; age comparison has no clean untreated group. Enjoyment was not measured.

shin.title: Shin et al.: decision quality & novelty
shin.summary: Reports higher engine-evaluated decision quality and earlier departures from historical sequences after superhuman AI. Tests several memorization explanations.
shin.locator: Figure 1A, PDF p.6; footnote p.7; tests pp.10–16
shin.limit: Analyzes the first 60 moves. Novelty is sequence-based. Supplemental figures and raw data were not independently reproduced.

earlier.title: Earlier human–AI gap study
earlier.date: Earlier paper linked by the player critique; evolving arXiv version
earlier.summary: Its stage-by-stage analysis places much of the measured improvement in the early game, especially moves 1–50.
earlier.locator: Figure 2 and adjacent discussion, PDF pp.4–5
earlier.limit: A stage-specific engine measure does not establish absence of all later-game learning or an enjoyment effect.

diversity.title: Choi et al.: knowledge & diversity
diversity.summary: Finds adoption of new local patterns and increased concentration in their use. Higher-skill professionals show stronger changes on these outcomes.
diversity.locator: Methods p.2; Figures 2–5 and discussion pp.3–5
diversity.limit: Eight-move local patterns; professional population. No explicit counterfactual control group. Less diversity does not imply less enjoyment.

critique.title: TuesdayBornWhale: learning critique
critique.summary: Challenges novelty and learning interpretations using local-pattern memorization, scope after move 60, and stage-dependent win-probability metrics. Raises concern about deference to AI.
critique.locator: “My critique,” “So… we aren’t getting better?” and appendix
critique.limit: No representative satisfaction survey or controlled reanalysis. Its individual cheating account is an author allegation, not independently verified here.

bessis.title: David Bessis: theorem economy
bessis.summary: Distinguishes mathematical understanding and meaning from theorem production, and questions analogies between mathematics and fixed-rule games.
bessis.locator: Opening argument; “The way of Go and Chess”
bessis.limit: Provides a lens on human value and incentives, not empirical evidence about Go enjoyment or participation.

ogs.title: OGS terms: computer help
ogs.summary: Prohibits engine analysis of ongoing games unless specifically permitted, and outside assistance in live or blitz games.
ogs.limit: Rules establish permitted conduct, not cheating prevalence or psychological effects.

ogsforum.title: OGS player fairness discussion
ogsforum.summary: A player raises suspected engine assistance and fairness; replies direct the player to reporting and platform rules.
ogsforum.limit: Self-selected anecdotal discussion. The allegation does not independently prove cheating or its frequency.

teachers.title: Trinks & Oh: teacher survey
teachers.summary: Educators report mixed views: non-use and concerns about suitability coexist with satisfaction among adopters.
teachers.locator: Journal abstract; full paper linked there
teachers.limit: Abstract checked. Teachers’ views concern education, not representative competitive online player enjoyment.

deepmind.title: DeepMind: AlphaGo Zero
deepmind.summary: Documents the progression beyond the AlphaGo version that defeated Lee Sedol and beyond Master, which defeated Ke Jie.
deepmind.locator: Opening research account and linked paper
deepmind.limit: Historical engine strength, not a current leaderboard or enjoyment study.

attack.title: Adversarial Go research
attack.summary: Shows exploitable strategies against specified superhuman engines that humans can replicate.
attack.limit: Attack success is conditional on evaluated systems and settings, not general human superiority.

humangames.title: Human exploit games and settings
humangames.date: Historical research examples; page checked October 12, 2026
humangames.summary: Reports Pelrine winning 14 of 15 games against JBXKata005 on KGS. Separately documents a win against KataGo at 100,000 visits using network b18c384nbt-uec.
humangames.locator: Human exploits KataGo; Human exploits a top KGS bot; linked game records
humangames.limit: The learned exploit tests robustness. Hardware and complete rule/time conditions are not specified in the visible summary. Not a current best-engine evaluation.

defense.title: Can Go AIs be adversarially robust?
defense.summary: Studies defenses and continuing adversarial weaknesses in tested Go AI systems.
defense.limit: A robustness test is distinct from ordinary competitive strength; no claim that every current engine is exploitable.

karlsson.title: Karlsson link in Brown’s reply
karlsson.summary: The observed source chain includes this link, but its article was unavailable.
karlsson.locator: Browser redirected to /go and displayed “Page not found”
karlsson.limit: Its content and attribution details were not inferred.
